details:
dlmm namesquats Meteora's real DLMM (Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker) SDK on Solana, published as a brand-new PyPI package with no relation to Meteora's actual SDK, which is not distributed under this exact PyPI name. `setup.py` contains top-level exec code that runs at install time (before any `import`), and `dlmm/__init__.py` runs the same install-time behavior again on first import, wrapped in a bare try/except so failures never surface to the user.

Sandbox execution confirmed the package reads `.npmrc` from the home directory (consistent with the same credential-harvesting template used by this actor's npm-side packages, which also scrape environment variables and SSH/Foundry/Hardhat/gcloud credential paths) and performs an outbound HTTP GET to a webhook.site endpoint immediately followed by a raw TCP connection to the same host on port 443 — an out-of-band callback confirming successful exfiltration to the operator.

This package shares the exact same webhook.site callback path as five other packages from the same actor published within the same short window on 2026-08-11 (`ethereum-vault-connector`, `@aerodrome-finance/contracts`, `@aerodrome-finance/slipstream`, `boring-vault`, `camelot-ammv2-core`, `camelot-ammv2-periphery` — all npm, all namesquatting real DeFi protocols) and a sibling PyPI package `dlmm-sdk`, also namesquatting Meteora's DLMM SDK. The package has since been removed from PyPI.

Any environment where this package was installed should be treated as having had its environment and reachable credential files exposed to the attacker; rotate all reachable secrets, especially PyPI/npm publish tokens and any wallet/RPC keys.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
